key_factors: (a)(3) tariff shift to heading 4412 (or 4421) from any other heading
decisive_step: Laminating and assembling the wood blocks and eucalyptus veneer into two-layer engineered flooring core panels in Canada
flip: If the wood blocks and veneer were laminated into panels prior to entering Canada and only cut to size in Canada without a tariff shift.
reasoning: The two-layer wood engineered flooring cores (lumber blocks of pine/basswood/SPF adhered to a eucalyptus veneer backing) are classified as laminated wood panels in heading 4412 (specifically 4412.99) or articles of wood in heading 4421, as they do not meet the definition of a veneered panel. Under 19 CFR 102.11(a)(3) and 102.20, the foreign eucalyptus veneer (4408) and lumber (4407/4409) undergo the required tariff shift to heading 4412/4421 when glued and pressed into two-layer panels in Canada.

decisive_step: Assembly and lamination of the face veneer, red pine lumber core, and eucalyptus backing into finished multilayer wood flooring panels in Canada
flip: Importing pre-assembled flooring panels of heading 4418 into Canada for only minor finishing or cutting
reasoning: Following the pattern of companion ruling N366014, the three-ply engineered wood flooring panels are classified in heading 4418 (specifically 4418.75 for multilayer assembled flooring panels per Additional U.S. Note 4(b) to Chapter 44). In Canada, the foreign and domestic wood components (veneers of heading 4408 and lumber core of heading 4407) are laminated into finished flooring panels. Because all foreign materials undergo the required tariff shift to heading 4418 from any other heading under 19 CFR 102.20(h), 102.11(a)(3) confers Canadian origin.

decisive_step: Cutting, drilling, staining, painting, and assembling the Russian birch plywood into tags in Canada
flip: Importing the wooden tags into Canada already pre-cut and pre-drilled (classifiable in heading 4421) for mere painting and attaching twine
reasoning: The finished personalized plywood gift tags are classified in heading 4421, HTSUS. The foreign Baltic birch plywood from Russia is classified in heading 4412. Under 19 CFR 102.20(h), the tariff shift rule for heading 4421 requires a change to heading 4421 from any other heading, except from sequential headings not applicable here. Because the Russian plywood shifts from heading 4412 to 4421 when cut, drilled, and finished in Canada, the country of origin is Canada pursuant to 19 CFR 102.11(a)(3).

decisive_step: Cutting, folding, interweaving, and gluing the paper materials into finished artwork in Canada
flip: If the artwork were pre-assembled in another country and only framed or packaged in Canada, it would not meet the tariff shift under 102.17.
reasoning: Consistent with the USMCA marking analysis in N365145, the country of origin of the paper artwork is determined under 19 CFR 102.11. Whether classified as original collages/assemblages under heading 9701 or other articles of paper under subheading 4823.90, transforming bulk paper strips and plastic backing by cutting, folding, interweaving, stacking, and adhering in Canada satisfies the applicable 19 CFR 102.20 tariff shift rule (change from any other heading/subheading). Thus, origin is conferred in Canada under 19 CFR 102.11(a)(3).

decisive_step: SMT population of the PCBs into PCBAs, final assembly with subassemblies, and firmware installation in France
flip: If the mainboard and backplane PCBAs were populated via SMT in China and merely enclosed in France, depending on whether the populated PCBA was already classified in the finished subheading or imparted essential character under 102.11(b)(1).
reasoning: The SRX server is a telecommunication/data processing apparatus (heading 8517 or 8471) packaged as a retail set with a power supply and cables. In France, bare PCBs and electronic components from various countries undergo SMT assembly to create the mainboard, backplane, and tray PCBAs, followed by integration with a Raspberry Pi module, enclosure, and firmware flashing. Under 19 CFR 102.11(a)(3), foreign components undergo the required 102.20 tariff shift (or under 102.11(b)(1), the French-made PCBAs impart the essential character).

decisive_step: Injection molding and finishing of U.S.-origin polypropylene resin into the wreath board in Canada
flip: If the wreath board were already molded in the United States and only underwent minor finishing or packing in Canada, the origin would be the United States.
reasoning: The finished wreath board is classified in subheading 3926.90, HTSUS. Under 19 CFR 102.11(a)(3), the applicable tariff shift rule in 19 CFR 102.20(g) for subheading 3926.90 requires a change to subheading 3926.10 through 3926.90 from any other heading, including another heading within that group. The U.S.-origin polypropylene plastic resin (classified in heading 3902) undergoes injection molding in Canada, shifting to heading 3926. Because all foreign materials satisfy the required tariff shift in Canada, the country of origin is Canada.

key_factors: (b) essential character of the ultrasonic flow meter (9026.10)
decisive_step: Manufacturing of the model D116 ultrasonic flow meter in China
flip: Manufacturing the ultrasonic flow meter (model D116) in Canada, or assembling the meter itself from parts (9026.90) in Canada so that all foreign materials undergo the required tariff shift under 102.20.
reasoning: The finished KRAKENmax flow meter is classified in subheading 9026.10. The 19 CFR 102.20 rule for 9026.10-9026.80 requires a change from any other subheading. The imported Chinese D116 ultrasonic flow meter is already a complete flow meter classified in subheading 9026.10. Because it fails to undergo a tariff shift when integrated with the wireless controller in Canada, rule 102.11(a)(3) is not met. Under 102.11(b) and 102.18(b), the non-shifting D116 flow meter imparts the essential character, conferring Chinese origin.

decisive_step: Cutting, assembling, and sewing the textile fabrics and obi sash materials into Christmas stockings in Canada
flip: If the stockings were cut and sewn in Japan and merely packaged in Canada, the origin would be Japan.
reasoning: Christmas stockings are classified as festive articles under subheading 9505.10, HTSUS, which is excluded from the textile rules of 19 CFR 102.21 and governed by 19 CFR 102.11. The foreign materials (vintage Japanese silk obi sashes of heading 6214/5007, cotton fabric of Ch. 52, and non-woven interfacing of heading 5603) are cut and sewn in Canada. Under 19 CFR 102.20(s), the rule for subheading 9505.10 requires a change from any other subheading. All foreign materials satisfy this tariff shift in Canada under 102.11(a)(3).

key_factors: (b) essential character of the thermal-coated jumbo paper roll
decisive_step: Manufacturing and thermal-coating of the jumbo paper rolls in Brazil
flip: Importing uncoated base paper of heading 4802 into Mexico and applying the thermal coating in Mexico, which would cause a tariff shift to heading 4811 under 102.11(a)(3).
reasoning: The finished thermal paper rolls and the imported Brazilian jumbo rolls are both classified in heading 4811 (subheadings 4811.90.80/90). Under 19 CFR 102.20(j), the rule for heading 4811 requires a change from any other heading (or for 4811.90 from any other subheading). Slitting 135.2cm rolls into 7.94cm rolls in Mexico does not change the heading or subheading, failing 102.11(a)(3). Under 102.11(b), the single material (the Brazilian thermal-coated paper roll) imparts the essential character, making Brazil the country of origin.

decisive_step: Fabrication of mounting brackets and complex assembly, integration, and testing of the pump, electrical, brush, and housing components in Canada
flip: If a foreign component classified in subheading 8479.89 (which fails the tariff shift) were imported into Canada and found to impart the essential character of the system
reasoning: The finished SkyOiler 360 is classified in subheading 8479.89, HTSUS. For a good of 8479.89, the 19 CFR 102.20(o) rule requires a change to subheading 8479.89 from any other subheading, including another subheading within heading 8479. The internationally sourced components (e.g., pump, motor, brushes, battery, charger, housing, and parts of 8479.90) are classified outside subheading 8479.89 and undergo the required tariff shift through fabrication and complex assembly in Canada, conferring Canadian origin under 19 CFR 102.11(a)(3).

decisive_step: Cutting, folding, designing, and assembling the paper into framed origami artwork in Canada
flip: If the origami figures were already cut and folded in China and only mounted into the frame in Canada
reasoning: As a decorative paper article excluded from Chapter 97, the origami artwork is classified under subheading 4823.90, HTSUS (consistent with paper artwork in N365695). For subheading 4823.90, 19 CFR 102.20(j) requires a change from any other subheading. The Chinese-origin paper sheets (headings 4802-4811) are cut, folded, and assembled into framed origami artwork in Canada, satisfying the required tariff shift under 19 CFR 102.11(a)(3) and conferring Canadian origin.

decisive_step: Slitting and rewinding jumbo rolls of silicone-coated paper (4811.59.20) into narrower consumer rolls measuring 12 to 15 inches wide (4811.59.40) in Canada
flip: If the imported rolls were already over 15 cm wide and exported in the same subheading without slitting across the 15 cm threshold, or if the coating and slitting both occurred in the source country
reasoning: Silicone-coated baking paper is excluded from heading 4806 and classified in heading 4811. Under heading 4811, jumbo rolls exceeding 15 cm in width fall in one subheading (e.g., 4811.59.20) while rolls 12-15 inches wide or cut to size shift subheadings (or under 19 CFR 102.20 for 4811, undergo a change from another heading/subheading when converted or coated in Canada). As in N366698, slitting jumbo coated paper rolls into smaller rolls satisfies the 102.20 tariff shift under 102.11(a)(3), conferring Canadian origin.

key_factors: (b) essential character of the glass bottle/vessel
decisive_step: Manufacture of the glass bottle/vessel in China
flip: Manufacturing the glass bottle/vessel in Slovenia
reasoning: The Kefirko Kefir Fermenter is a composite good or retail set classified under heading 7013 (glassware for table/kitchen purposes) because the glass vessel imparts its essential character under GRI 3(b). Under 19 CFR 102.11(a)(3), the 102.20 rule for heading 7013 requires a change from any other heading (except certain headings of chapter 70). The Chinese glass bottle is already classified in heading 7013 and fails to shift during simple assembly/packaging in Slovenia (102.17). Under 102.11(b), the glass vessel imparts the essential character, conferring Chinese origin.
